    57→
    58→def _prune_stale_triage_meta(
    59→    plan: PlanModel,
    60→    *,
    61→    stale_ids: set[str],
    62→) -> None:
    63→    """Drop stale review IDs from triage recovery metadata."""

    66→        return
    67→
    68→    active_ids = meta.get("active_triage_issue_ids")
    69→    if isinstance(active_ids, list):
    70→        filtered_active = [
    71→            issue_id for issue_id in active_ids
    72→            if isinstance(issue_id, str) and issue_id not in stale_ids
    73→        ]
    74→        if filtered_active:

    76→        else:

    82→            issue_id for issue_id in undispositioned_ids
    83→            if isinstance(issue_id, str) and issue_id not in stale_ids
    84→        ]

    87→            meta["undispositioned_issue_count"] = len(filtered_undispositioned)

    93→def _prune_stale_review_ids_from_plan(
    94→    plan: PlanModel,
    95→    *,

    97→) -> list[str]:
    98→    """Remove stale review IDs from queue-related plan containers.
    99→
   100→    Review imports can auto-resolve prior review IDs. These IDs must be removed
   101→    from queue_order (and linked queue metadata) or the queue can drift from
   102→    state reality.
   103→    """
   104→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   105→    stale_ids = sorted(
   106→        {
   107→            issue_id
   108→            for issue_id in order
   109→            if _is_review_queue_id(issue_id) and issue_id not in live_open_review_ids
   110→        }
   111→    )
   112→    if not stale_ids:
   113→        return []
   114→
   115→    stale_set = set(stale_ids)
   116→    order[:] = [issue_id for issue_id in order if issue_id not in stale_set]
   117→    prune_promoted_ids(plan, stale_set)
   118→    _prune_stale_triage_meta(plan, stale_ids=stale_set)
   119→
   120→    deferred = plan.get("deferred")
   121→    if isinstance(deferred, list):
   122→        plan["deferred"] = [issue_id for issue_id in deferred if issue_id not in stale_set]
   123→
   124→    skipped = plan.get("skipped")
   125→    if isinstance(skipped, dict):
   126→        for issue_id in stale_set:
   127→            skipped.pop(issue_id, None)
   128→
   129→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   130→        issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids")
   131→        if not isinstance(issue_ids, list):
   132→            continue
   133→        cluster["issue_ids"] = [
   134→            issue_id for issue_id in issue_ids if issue_id not in stale_set
   135→        ]
   136→
   137→    return stale_ids
   138→
   139→
   140→def sync_plan_after_review_import(
   141→    plan: PlanModel,
   142→    state: StateModel,
   143→    *,
   144→    policy=None,
   145→) -> ReviewImportSyncResult | None:
   146→    """Sync plan queue after review import. Pure engine function — no I/O.
   147→
   148→    Appends new issue IDs to queue_order, prunes stale review IDs from queue
   149→    containers, and injects triage stages if needed (respects mid-cycle guard
   150→    — defers when objective work remains). Returns ``None`` when no queue
   151→    changes are required.
   152→    """
   153→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   154→    open_review_ids = compute_open_issue_ids(state)
   155→    stale_pruned_from_queue = _prune_stale_review_ids_from_plan(
   156→        plan,
   157→        live_open_review_ids=open_review_ids,
   158→    )
   159→    new_ids = _review_issue_ids_for_import_sync(
   160→        plan,
   161→        state,
   162→        open_review_ids=open_review_ids,
   163→    )
   164→    if not new_ids and not stale_pruned_from_queue:
   165→        return None
   166→
   167→    # Add new issue IDs to end of queue_order so they have position
   168→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   169→    existing = set(order)
   170→    added: list[str] = []
   171→    for issue_id in sorted(new_ids):
   172→        if issue_id not in existing:
   173→            order.append(issue_id)
   174→            added.append(issue_id)
   175→
   176→    # Inject triage stages if needed (policy enables mid-cycle guard)
   177→    triage_result = sync_triage_needed(plan, state, policy=policy)
   178→    triage_injected_ids = list(getattr(triage_result, "injected", []) or [])
   179→    triage_injected = bool(triage_injected_ids)
   180→    triage_deferred = bool(triage_result and getattr(triage_result, "deferred", False))
   181→
   182→    return ReviewImportSyncResult(
   183→        new_ids=new_ids,
   184→        added_to_queue=added,
   185→        stale_pruned_from_queue=stale_pruned_from_queue,
   186→        triage_injected=triage_injected,
   187→        triage_injected_ids=triage_injected_ids,
   188→        triage_deferred=triage_deferred,
   189→    )
   190→
   191→

   160→    plan: PlanModel,
   161→    state: StateModel,
   162→    *,
   163→    referenced_ids: set[str],
   164→    now: str,
   165→    result: ReconcileResult,
   166→) -> None:
   167→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   168→        if _is_issue_alive(state, fid):
   169→            continue
   170→        if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   171→            result.superseded.append(fid)
   172→            result.changes += 1
   173→

   175→def _complete_empty_manual_clusters(
   176→    plan: PlanModel,
   177→    *,
   178→    pre_sizes: dict[str, int],
   179→    result: ReconcileResult,
   180→) -> None:
   181→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   182→    for name, prev_size in pre_sizes.items():
   183→        if prev_size == 0:
   184→            continue
   185→        cluster = clusters.get(name)
   186→        if cluster is None or len(cluster.get("issue_ids", [])) != 0:
   187→            continue
   188→        result.clusters_completed.append(name)
   189→        append_log_entry(
   190→            plan,
   191→            "cluster_done",
   192→            issue_ids=[],
   193→            cluster_name=name,
   194→            actor="system",
   195→            detail={"reason": "cluster members no longer actionable in state"},
   196→        )

   210→            continue
   211→        issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   212→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if _is_issue_alive(state, fid)]
   213→        if alive_ids != issue_ids:
   214→            cluster["issue_ids"] = alive_ids
   215→            result.changes += 1
   216→        if not alive_ids:
   217→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   218→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   219→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   220→        result.changes += 1

   223→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   224→    plan: PlanModel,
   225→    state: StateModel,
   226→) -> ReconcileResult:
   227→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   228→
   229→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   230→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   231→    """
   232→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   233→    result = ReconcileResult()
   234→    now = utc_now()
   235→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   236→
   237→    referenced_ids = _referenced_plan_issue_ids(plan)
   238→
   239→    # Snapshot non-epic cluster sizes before superseding so we can detect
   240→    # clusters that become empty after state reconciliation.
   241→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   242→    pre_sizes: dict[str, int] = {
   243→        name: len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   244→        for name, cluster in clusters.items()
   245→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   246→    }
   247→
   248→    _supersede_dead_references(
   249→        plan,
   250→        state,
   251→        referenced_ids=referenced_ids,
   252→        now=now,
   253→        result=result,
   254→    )
   255→    _complete_empty_manual_clusters(plan, pre_sizes=pre_sizes, result=result)
   256→    _reconcile_epic_clusters(plan, state, result=result)
   257→
   258→    clear_focus_if_cluster_empty(plan)
   259→
   260→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   261→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   262→
   263→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   264→    if resurfaced:
   265→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   266→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   267→
   268→    # Prune old superseded entries
   269→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   270→    result.pruned = pruned
   271→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   272→
   273→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   274→    if result.changes > 0:
   275→        append_log_entry(
   276→            plan,
   277→            "reconcile",
   278→            issue_ids=result.superseded,
   279→            actor="system",
   280→            detail={
   281→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   282→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   283→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   284→                "clusters_completed_count": len(result.clusters_completed),
   285→            },
   286→        )
   287→
   288→    return result
   289→

    51→def _load_state_with_guards(
    52→    args: argparse.Namespace,

    54→    attestation: str | None,
    55→) -> tuple[str, dict, object] | None:
    56→    """Validate inputs, apply guardrails, and load state for resolve."""

    78→            attest=getattr(args, "attest", "") or "",

    81→    return state_file, state, plan_access

   114→def cmd_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   115→    """Resolve issue(s) matching one or more patterns."""
   116→    attestation = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   117→    loaded = _load_state_with_guards(args, attestation=attestation)
   118→    if loaded is None:
   119→        return
   120→    state_file, state, plan_access = loaded
   121→    prev, prev_subjective_scores, all_resolved = _resolve_ids_with_snapshots(
   122→        state,
   123→        args,
   124→        attestation=attestation,
   125→        plan_access=plan_access,
   126→    )
   127→    if not all_resolved:
   128→        print_no_match_warning(args)
   129→        return
   130→
   131→    save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)
   132→
   133→    plan, cluster_ctx = update_living_plan_after_resolve(
   134→        args=args,
   135→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   136→        attestation=attestation,
   137→        state_file=state_file,
   138→    )
   139→    mid_cluster = (
   140→        cluster_ctx.cluster_name is not None and not cluster_ctx.cluster_completed
   141→    )
   142→
   143→    _print_resolve_summary(status=args.status, all_resolved=all_resolved)
   144→    _print_wontfix_batch_warning(
   145→        state,
   146→        status=args.status,
   147→        resolved_count=len(all_resolved),
   148→    )
   149→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   150→    if not mid_cluster:
   151→        render_commit_guidance(state, plan, all_resolved, args.status)
   152→    _print_subjective_reset_hint(
   153→        args=args,
   154→        state=state,
   155→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   156→        prev_subjective_scores=prev_subjective_scores,
   157→    )
   158→
   159→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   160→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   161→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(
   162→        state,
   163→        context=narrative_mod.NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="resolve"),
   164→    )
   165→    if narrative.get("milestone"):
   166→        print(colorize(f"  → {narrative['milestone']}", "green"))
   167→
   168→    next_command = _print_next_command(state)
   169→    _write_resolve_query_entry(
   170→        ResolveQueryContext(
   171→            patterns=args.patterns,
   172→            status=args.status,
   173→            resolved=all_resolved,
   174→            next_command=next_command,
   175→            prev_overall=prev.overall,
   176→            prev_objective=prev.objective,
   177→            prev_strict=prev.strict,
   178→            prev_verified=prev.verified,
   179→            attestation=attestation,

    10→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
    11→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    12→from desloppify.app.commands.resolve.plan_load import warn_plan_load_degraded_once
    13→from desloppify.engine.plan_ops import (

    17→)

    19→from desloppify.engine.plan_state import (
    20→    add_uncommitted_issues,
    21→    has_living_plan,

    25→    save_plan,

    28→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    29→
    30→
    31→class ClusterContext(NamedTuple):
    32→    cluster_name: str | None
    33→    cluster_completed: bool
    34→    cluster_remaining: int
    35→
    36→
    37→def capture_cluster_context(plan: dict, resolved_ids: list[str]) -> ClusterContext:
    38→    """Determine cluster membership for resolved issues before purge."""
    39→    clusters = plan.get("clusters") or {}
    40→    overrides = plan.get("overrides") or {}
    41→    cluster_name: str | None = None
    42→    for resolved_id in resolved_ids:
    43→        override = overrides.get(resolved_id)
    44→        if override and override.get("cluster"):
    45→            cluster_name = override["cluster"]
    46→            break
    47→    if not cluster_name or cluster_name not in clusters:
    48→        return ClusterContext(cluster_name=None, cluster_completed=False, cluster_remaining=0)
    49→    current_ids = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids") or [])
    50→    remaining = current_ids - set(resolved_ids)
    51→    return ClusterContext(
    52→        cluster_name=cluster_name,
    53→        cluster_completed=len(remaining) == 0,
    54→        cluster_remaining=len(remaining),
    55→    )
    56→
    57→
    58→def update_living_plan_after_resolve(
    59→    *,
    60→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    61→    all_resolved: list[str],
    62→    attestation: str | None,
    63→    state_file: Path | str | None = None,
    64→) -> tuple[dict | None, ClusterContext]:
    65→    """Apply resolve side effects to the living plan when it exists."""
    66→    plan_path = plan_path_for_state(Path(state_file)) if state_file else None
    67→    plan = None
    68→    ctx = ClusterContext(cluster_name=None, cluster_completed=False, cluster_remaining=0)
    69→    try:
    70→        if not has_living_plan(plan_path):
    71→            return None, ctx
    72→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
    73→        ctx = capture_cluster_context(plan, all_resolved)
    74→        purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)
    75→        step_messages = auto_complete_steps(plan)
    76→        for msg in step_messages:
    77→            print(colorize(msg, "green"))
    78→        append_log_entry(
    79→            plan,
    80→            "resolve",
    81→            issue_ids=all_resolved,
    82→            actor="user",
    83→            note=getattr(args, "note", None),
    84→            detail={"status": args.status, "attestation": attestation},
    85→        )
    86→        if ctx.cluster_completed and ctx.cluster_name:
    87→            append_log_entry(
    88→                plan,
    89→                "cluster_done",
    90→                issue_ids=all_resolved,
    91→                cluster_name=ctx.cluster_name,
    92→                actor="user",
    93→            )
    94→        if args.status == "fixed":
    95→            add_uncommitted_issues(plan, all_resolved)
    96→        elif args.status == "open":
    97→            purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, all_resolved)
    98→        clear_postflight_scan_completion(plan, issue_ids=all_resolved)
    99→        save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   100→        if purged:
   101→            print(colorize(f"  Plan updated: {purged} item(s) removed from queue.", "dim"))
   102→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   103→        _logger.debug("plan update failed after resolve", exc_info=True)
   104→        warn_plan_load_degraded_once(
   105→            command_label="resolve",
   106→            error_kind=exc.__class__.__name__,
   107→            behavior="Living-plan queue metadata could not be updated after resolve.",
   108→        )
   109→    return plan, ctx
   110→
   111→
   112→__all__ = ["ClusterContext", "capture_cluster_context", "update_living_plan_after_resolve"]
   113→

## Summary: State Issue Status and Plan Skip Status Synchronization

Based on my thorough investigation of the codebase, here's the complete picture of how these two systems interact:

### **Key Findings:**

#### **1. When `plan skip --permanent` creates a skip:**
- **YES**, it also sets `issue.status = "wontfix"` in state
- The `_apply_state_skip_resolution()` function in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py` (lines 80-100) calls `skip_kind_state_status(kind)` which returns `"wontfix"` for permanent skips
- Then `resolve_issues(state_data, fid, "wontfix", ...)` is called, which updates the issue status (line 93)
- The plan skip is created separately via `skip_items(plan, issue_ids, kind="permanent", ...)`

#### **2. When `plan skip --false-positive` creates a skip:**
- **YES**, it also sets `issue.status = "false_positive"` in state
- Same flow as permanent: `skip_kind_state_status("false_positive")` returns `"false_positive"`
- The state is updated via `resolve_issues()` before the plan skip is created

#### **3. When `plan skip` (temporary) creates a skip:**
- **NO**, issue status remains `"open"` in state
- The policy function `skip_kind_state_status("temporary")` returns `None` (skip_policy.py, line 47)
- Therefore `_apply_state_skip_resolution()` returns `None` early and no state update happens (line 89-90)
- The issue stays `status: "open"` but is moved to `plan["skipped"]` with `kind: "temporary"`

#### **4. Can an issue be `status: "open"` with a `temporary` skip in plan?**
- **YES**, and this is the normal, intended state
- A `temporary` skip is for deferring work — the issue is still considered "open" but is hidden from the active queue
- The issue can resurface if `review_after` threshold is hit (via `resurface_stale_skips()` in skip.py, lines 146-169)

#### **5. When issues are auto-resolved (`auto_resolved` status):**
- **NO corresponding plan skip is created**
- Auto-resolved happens via `auto_resolve_review_issues()` in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/importing/resolution.py` (lines 11-37)
- It sets `issue["status"] = "fixed"` with `resolution_attestation.kind = "agent_import"`
- No plan skip is created; instead, stale review IDs are removed from queue (reconcile_review_import.py, lines 124-127)
- The stale IDs are pruned from `plan["skipped"]` dict (line 126-127)

#### **6. Reconciliation in `_plan/sync/` modules:**
- **Partial reconciliation occurs**: After review imports, stale review issue IDs are pruned from plan skipped dict (reconcile_review_import.py, lines 124-127)
- There is **NO bidirectional sync**: changing `issue.status` to `wontfix` via another path does NOT auto-create a plan skip
- The sync is one-way: plan skip operations → state status updates (via override_skip.py)

#### **7. User-facing skip flow in `override_skip.py`:**
- The `cmd_plan_skip()` function (line 180) orchestrates the complete flow:
  1. Call `_apply_state_skip_resolution()` — updates state status if kind is "permanent" or "false_positive"
  2. Call `skip_items(plan, ...)` — creates the plan skip entry
  3. Save both plan and state transactionally via `save_plan_state_transactional()`

#### **8. Where `issue.status` gets set to `wontfix`/`false_positive`:**
- **Only via plan skip command** (override_skip.py, `_apply_state_skip_resolution()`)
- **OR via manual `plan resolve` command** (uses `resolve_issues()` from engine/_state/resolution.py)
- **OR via auto-merge in review importing** (sets status to `"fixed"`, not "wontfix")
- There is **no other path** that creates corresponding plan skips

#### **9. Review import plan sync (`plan_sync.py`):**
- Does **NOT sync issue statuses to plan skips**
- Only syncs queue_order and removes stale review IDs from plan containers
- Focuses on maintaining queue consistency after auto-resolved duplicates disappear from state

### **Can They Drift Apart?**

**YES — Partial drift is possible:**

1. **If `issue.status = "wontfix"` is set via `resolve_issues()` directly** (e.g., through `desloppify fix` or manual state editing), **no plan skip is created**
   - Issue is marked wontfix in state but remains in queue or unmarked in plan
   - The unskip command (line 294) has logic to reopen these: `skip_kind_needs_state_reopen()` checks if a skip kind is "permanent" or "false_positive", and if so, calls `resolve_issues(state_data, fid, "open")` on unskip

2. **If an issue with a `temporary` skip survives auto-resolution**, it won't be auto-removed from skipped dict
   - Review import only prunes skips for review IDs (line 124-127)
   - Other issue types with temporary skips stay in skipped dict even if their state is later marked fixed

3. **If plan is mutated outside the CLI flow**, state and plan can diverge
   - There's no sync loop that continuously reconciles the two

### **Conclusion:**

These systems are **partially synchronized**:
- **Strong sync on write**: When you use `plan skip --permanent/--false-positive`, both state and plan are updated transactionally
- **Weak or no sync in reverse**: Setting `issue.status` directly does not auto-create plan skips
- **Automatic recovery on unskip**: The unskip command knows to reopen permanently/false-positive-skipped issues in state
- **Temporary skips are intentionally asymmetric**: Issue stays "open" in state while hidden in plan — this is by design

The codebase does **not guarantee strict consistency** across all paths, but the primary user-facing path (plan skip/unskip) maintains transactional consistency.

## Complete Mapping of Code Paths Where `issue["status"]` Gets Changed

Based on my comprehensive search, here are ALL the paths in the codebase where issue status is mutated:

- **`resolve_holistic_coverage_issues()`** (line 144): Marks dimension-level subjective_review issues fixed
  - Sets `issue["status"] = "fixed"`
  - Creates `resolution_attestation` with `kind: "agent_import"`

#### **1d. Review Merge Duplicate Handling** (`desloppify/app/commands/review/merge.py`)
- **`merge_duplicate_review_issues()`** (line 212): Marks conceptually duplicate issues as auto-resolved
  - Sets `duplicate["status"] = "auto_resolved"`
  - Creates `resolution_attestation` with `kind: "issue_merge"`

#### **1e. Autofix Results Processing** (`desloppify/app/commands/autofix/apply_retro.py`)
- **`_resolve_fixer_results()`** (line 28): Marks successfully fixed items resolved
  - Sets `state["issues"][issue_id]["status"] = "fixed"`

#### **1f. Schema Normalization** (`desloppify/engine/_state/schema.py`, line 208)
- **`ensure_state_defaults()`**: Canonicalizes status on load
  - `issue["status"] = canonical_issue_status(...)`

#### **1g. Manual Resolution Commands** (`desloppify/engine/_state/resolution.py`)
- **`resolve_issues()`** (lines 113-215): Core manual resolution function
  - Sets `issue["status"] = status` where status can be `"fixed"`, `"wontfix"`, or `"open"` (line 183)
  - Handles reopening (lines 165-180): Creates `resolution_attestation` with `kind: "manual_reopen"`
  - Handles closing (lines 189-195): Creates `resolution_attestation` with `kind: "manual"`
  - Also calls `_mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve()` for review issue resolution

### **2. PLAN-LEVEL SYNCHRONIZATION (where plan.skipped gets synchronized)**

#### **2a. Plan Skip Operations** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/skip.py`)
- **`skip_items()`** (lines 65-97): Moves issue IDs from queue to skipped dict
  - Creates entries in `plan["skipped"]` with metadata (kind, reason, etc.)
- **`unskip_items()`** (lines 111-143): Moves IDs back from skipped to queue_order
  - Includes `skip_kind_needs_state_reopen()` logic to reopen state-layer issues
- **`resurface_stale_skips()`** (lines 146-169): Auto-resurrects temporary skips past review_after threshold
  - Removes from `plan["skipped"]` and adds back to `queue_order`
- **`backlog_items()`** (lines 172-184): Removes from plan.skipped without re-queuing

#### **2b. Plan Triage Dismissal** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/dismiss.py`)
- **`dismiss_triage_issues()`** (lines 28-69): Epic triage dismisses issues
  - Creates entries in `skipped` dict with `kind: "triaged_out"`
  - Removes from `order` list

#### **2c. Plan Reconciliation After Scan** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/reconcile.py`)
- **`reconcile_plan_after_scan()`** (lines 223-288): Post-scan sync of plan with state
  - **`_supersede_dead_references()`** (lines 159-172): Moves disappeared issues to superseded
    - Calls `_supersede_id()` which removes from both `queue_order` AND `plan["skipped"]` (lines 100-104)
  - **`_reconcile_epic_clusters()`** (lines 200-220): Updates cluster membership based on issue state

#### **2d. Plan Purge Operations** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/operations/lifecycle.py`)
- **`purge_ids()`** (lines 62-97): Removes issue IDs completely from plan
  - Removes from `order` list (line 80)
  - **Removes from `plan["skipped"]` dict (lines 82-83)** ← KEY SYNC POINT
  - Removes from cluster memberships (lines 85-89)

#### **2e. Plan Resolve Side Effects** (`desloppify/app/commands/resolve/living_plan.py`)
- **`update_living_plan_after_resolve()`** (lines 58-109): Called after any resolve command
  - Calls **`purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)`** (line 74) ← This removes from plan.skipped
  - Handles `add_uncommitted_issues()` for "fixed" status (line 95)
  - Handles `purge_uncommitted_ids()` for "open" status (line 97)

#### **2f. Plan Schema Migrations** (`desloppify/engine/_plan/schema/version_upgrades.py`)
- **`migrate_deferred_to_skipped()`** (lines 30-51): Data migration for legacy "deferred" → "skipped"
  - Creates skipped entries from deferred IDs
  - Updates issue_id keys when issues are renamed (lines 137-140)

### **3. KEY SYNCHRONIZATION GUARANTEE**

**CRITICAL FINDING**: The synchronization between `issue["status"]` and `plan["skipped"]` happens through `purge_ids()`:

```
resolve command (fixes/wontfix/reopens issue)
  ↓
resolve_issues() changes issue["status"] in state
  ↓
save_state()
  ↓
update_living_plan_after_resolve() calls purge_ids()
  ↓
purge_ids() removes from plan["skipped"] (lines 82-83)
```

**When status changes to non-open**: Issue stays in queue_order or gets added to skipped via `skip_items()`
**When status changes to open**: Issue is purged from plan entirely (queue_order + skipped both)

### **4. LOCATIONS WITHOUT AUTOMATIC SYNCHRONIZATION**

These are cases where issue["status"] changes but plan.skipped may NOT be automatically updated:

1. **Auto-resolve via import** (`auto_resolve_review_issues`, `resolve_holistic_coverage_issues`):
   - Changes `issue["status"] = "fixed"` in state
   - BUT doesn't call `purge_ids()` on plan
   - Plan reconciliation happens later (at next scan/plan reload)

2. **Autofix cascade resolution** (`_resolve_fixer_results`):
   - Changes `issue["status"] = "fixed"` in state
   - BUT doesn't update plan synchronously
   - Requires explicit plan reconciliation

3. **Merge duplicates** (`merge_duplicate_review_issues`):
   - Changes `duplicate["status"] = "auto_resolved"`
   - BUT doesn't remove from plan.skipped automatically
   - Relies on plan reconciliation on next load

### **ANSWER TO YOUR CORE QUESTION**

**Is `plan.skipped` always updated in parallel when `issue["status"]` changes?**

**NO** — synchronization is **eventual, not immediate**:
- Direct user commands (resolve/reopen) → **immediate sync via `purge_ids()`**
- Automatic imports (holistic, merge, autofix) → **deferred sync on next plan reconciliation**
- Disappearance from scan → **reconciliation moves to superseded (removes from skipped)**

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

     6→SYSTEM_SKIP_KINDS = ("triaged_out",)

    22→def skip_kind_from_flags(*, permanent: bool, false_positive: bool) -> str:
    23→    """Map CLI flags to a canonical skip kind."""
    24→    if false_positive:
    25→        return "false_positive"
    26→    if permanent:
    27→        return "permanent"
    28→    return "temporary"
    29→
    30→
    31→def skip_kind_requires_attestation(kind: str) -> bool:
    32→    """Return True when the skip kind requires attestation text."""
    33→    return kind in {"permanent", "false_positive"}
    34→
    35→
    36→def skip_kind_requires_note(kind: str) -> bool:
    37→    """Return True when the skip kind requires a user note."""
    38→    return kind == "permanent"

    41→def skip_kind_state_status(kind: str) -> str | None:

1→"""Issue upsert/verification helpers for scan merge."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import matches_exclusion
     6→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import matched_ignore_pattern
     7→
     8→
     9→def find_suspect_detectors(
    10→    existing: dict,
    11→    current_by_detector: dict[str, int],
    12→    force_resolve: bool,
    13→    ran_detectors: set[str] | None = None,
    14→) -> set[str]:
    15→    """Detectors that had open issues but likely did not actually run this scan."""
    16→    if force_resolve:
    17→        return set()
    18→
    19→    previous_open_by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
    20→    for issue in existing.values():
    21→        if issue["status"] != "open":
    22→            continue
    23→        detector = issue.get("detector", "unknown")
    24→        previous_open_by_detector[detector] = (
    25→            previous_open_by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
    26→        )
    27→
    28→    # 'review' issues enter via `desloppify review --import`, not via scan phases.
    29→    # They are always suspect so the scan never auto-resolves them — regardless
    30→    # of current issue status (open, wontfix, etc.).
    31→    import_only_detectors = {"review"}
    32→    suspect: set[str] = set(import_only_detectors)
    33→
    34→    for detector, previous_count in previous_open_by_detector.items():
    35→        if detector in import_only_detectors:
    36→            continue
    37→        if current_by_detector.get(detector, 0) > 0:
    38→            continue
    39→        if ran_detectors is not None:
    40→            if detector not in ran_detectors:
    41→                suspect.add(detector)
    42→            continue
    43→        if previous_count >= 3:
    44→            suspect.add(detector)
    45→
    46→    return suspect
    47→
    48→
    49→def _mark_scan_verified(
    50→    issue: dict,
    51→    now: str,
    52→    *,
    53→    note: str,
    54→    attestation_text: str,
    55→) -> None:
    56→    """Record scan corroboration without changing the manual disposition."""
    57→    issue["suppressed"] = False
    58→    issue["suppressed_at"] = None
    59→    issue["suppression_pattern"] = None
    60→    issue["note"] = note
    61→    existing = issue.get("resolution_attestation")
    62→    if not isinstance(existing, dict):
    63→        existing = {}
    64→        issue["resolution_attestation"] = existing
    65→    existing["scan_verified"] = True
    66→    existing["scan_verified_at"] = now
    67→    existing["scan_verification_text"] = attestation_text
    68→
    69→
    70→def verify_disappeared(
    71→    existing: dict,
    72→    current_ids: set[str],
    73→    suspect_detectors: set[str],
    74→    now: str,
    75→    *,
    76→    lang: str | None,
    77→    scan_path: str | None,
    78→    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    79→) -> tuple[int, int, int, set[str]]:
    80→    """Update scan corroboration for issues absent from scan.
    81→
    82→    Returns (resolved_count, skipped_other_lang, resolved_out_of_scope, changed_detectors).
    83→    Queue-tracked work stays user-controlled: disappearing from scan does not
    84→    change an open issue to resolved. Manually resolved items can be marked as
    85→    scan-verified when they remain absent.
    86→    """
    87→    resolved = skipped_other_lang = resolved_out_of_scope = 0
    88→    resolved_detectors: set[str] = set()
    89→
    90→    for issue_id, previous in existing.items():
    91→        previous_status = previous.get("status")
    92→        if issue_id in current_ids or previous_status not in (
    93→            "open",
    94→            "wontfix",
    95→            "fixed",
    96→            "false_positive",
    97→        ):
    98→            continue
    99→
   100→        if lang and previous.get("lang") and previous["lang"] != lang:
   101→            skipped_other_lang += 1
   102→            continue
   103→
   104→        # Suspect detectors (e.g. 'review') are import-only and must never
   105→        # be auto-resolved by a scan — check this BEFORE the scope filter
   106→        # so that review issues with file="." aren't wrongly resolved as
   107→        # "out of current scan scope".
   108→        if previous.get("detector", "unknown") in suspect_detectors:
   109→            continue
   110→
   111→        if scan_path and scan_path != ".":
   112→            prefix = scan_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
   113→            if (
   114→                not previous["file"].startswith(prefix)
   115→                and previous["file"] != scan_path
   116→            ):
   117→                if previous_status != "open":
   118→                    scope_note = f"Still absent in current scan scope ({scan_path})"
   119→                    _mark_scan_verified(
   120→                        previous,
   121→                        now,
   122→                        note=scope_note,
   123→                        attestation_text=scope_note,
   124→                    )
   125→                    resolved_detectors.add(previous.get("detector", "unknown"))
   126→                    resolved_out_of_scope += 1
   127→                continue
   128→
   129→        if exclude and any(matches_exclusion(previous["file"], ex) for ex in exclude):
   130→            continue
   131→
   132→        if previous_status == "open":
   133→            continue
   134→
   135→        verification_note = (
   136→            "Still absent from scan after manual wontfix"
   137→            if previous_status == "wontfix"
   138→            else "Still absent from scan after manual resolution"
   139→        )
   140→        _mark_scan_verified(
   141→            previous,
   142→            now,
   143→            note=verification_note,
   144→            attestation_text="Absent from detector output in latest scan",
   145→        )
   146→        resolved_detectors.add(previous.get("detector", "unknown"))
   147→        resolved += 1
   148→
   149→    return resolved, skipped_other_lang, resolved_out_of_scope, resolved_detectors
   150→
   151→
   152→def upsert_issues(
   153→    existing: dict,
   154→    current_issues: list[dict],
   155→    ignore: list[str],
   156→    now: str,
   157→    *,
   158→    lang: str | None,
   159→) -> tuple[set[str], int, int, dict[str, int], int, set[str]]:
   160→    """Insert new issues and update existing ones.
   161→
   162→    Returns (current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, by_detector, ignored_count, changed_detectors).
   163→    """
   164→    current_ids: set[str] = set()
   165→    new_count = reopened_count = ignored_count = 0
   166→    by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
   167→    changed_detectors: set[str] = set()
   168→
   169→    for issue in current_issues:
   170→        issue_id = issue["id"]
   171→        detector = issue.get("detector", "unknown")
   172→        current_ids.add(issue_id)
   173→        by_detector[detector] = by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
   174→        matched_ignore = matched_ignore_pattern(issue_id, issue["file"], ignore)
   175→        if matched_ignore:
   176→            ignored_count += 1
   177→
   178→        if lang:
   179→            issue["lang"] = lang
   180→
   181→        if issue_id not in existing:
   182→            existing[issue_id] = dict(issue)
   183→            if matched_ignore:
   184→                existing[issue_id]["suppressed"] = True
   185→                existing[issue_id]["suppressed_at"] = now
   186→                existing[issue_id]["suppression_pattern"] = matched_ignore
   187→                continue
   188→            new_count += 1
   189→            changed_detectors.add(detector)
   190→            continue
   191→
   192→        previous = existing[issue_id]
   193→        previous.update(
   194→            last_seen=now,
   195→            tier=issue["tier"],
   196→            confidence=issue["confidence"],
   197→            summary=issue["summary"],
   198→            detail=issue.get("detail", {}),
   199→        )
   200→        if "zone" in issue:
   201→            previous["zone"] = issue["zone"]
   202→        if lang and not previous.get("lang"):
   203→            previous["lang"] = lang
   204→
   205→        if matched_ignore:
   206→            previous["suppressed"] = True
   207→            previous["suppressed_at"] = now
   208→            previous["suppression_pattern"] = matched_ignore
   209→            continue
   210→
   211→        previous["suppressed"] = False
   212→        previous["suppressed_at"] = None
   213→        previous["suppression_pattern"] = None
   214→
   215→        if previous["status"] in ("fixed", "auto_resolved", "false_positive"):
   216→            # subjective_review issues are condition-based.  When just
   217→            # completed by an agent import, skip reopening to avoid a
   218→            # resolve-then-reopen loop on the same scan cycle.
   219→            if (
   220→                detector == "subjective_review"
   221→                and previous["status"] in {"fixed", "auto_resolved"}
   222→                and (previous.get("resolution_attestation") or {}).get("kind") == "agent_import"
   223→            ):
   224→                continue
   225→            previous_status = previous["status"]
   226→            previous["reopen_count"] = previous.get("reopen_count", 0) + 1
   227→            previous.pop("resolution_attestation", None)
   228→            previous.update(
   229→                status="open",
   230→                resolved_at=None,
   231→                note=(
   232→                    f"Reopened (×{previous['reopen_count']}) "
   233→                    f"— reappeared in scan (was {previous_status})"
   234→                ),
   235→            )
   236→            reopened_count += 1
   237→            changed_detectors.add(detector)
   238→
   239→    return current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, by_detector, ignored_count, changed_detectors
   240→
   241→
   242→__all__ = [
   243→    "verify_disappeared",
   244→    "find_suspect_detectors",
   245→    "upsert_issues",
   246→]
   247→

     5→from collections import defaultdict
     6→from typing import Any

     8→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel

    10→
    11→def _open_issues(state: StateModel) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    12→    """Return all open issues from state."""
    13→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    14→    return [
    15→        finding for finding in issues.values()
    16→        if isinstance(finding, dict) and finding.get("status") == "open"
    17→    ]
    18→
    19→
    20→def _group_by_file(state: StateModel) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    21→    """Group open issues by file, excluding holistic (file='.') issues."""
    22→    by_file: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = defaultdict(list)
    23→    for finding in _open_issues(state):
    24→        file = finding.get("file", "")
    25→        if file and file != ".":
    26→            by_file[file].append(finding)
    27→    return dict(by_file)
    28→
    29→
    30→__all__ = ["_group_by_file", "_open_issues"]
    31→

    16→def _analyze_dimensions(dim_scores: dict, history: list[dict], state: StateModel) -> dict:
    17→    """Compute per-dimension structured analysis."""
    18→    if not dim_scores:
    19→        return {}
    20→
    21→    potentials = merge_potentials(state.get("potentials", {}))
    22→    return {
    23→        "lowest_dimensions": _lowest_dimensions(dim_scores, potentials),
    24→        "biggest_gap_dimensions": _biggest_gap_dimensions(dim_scores, state)[:3],

    29→def _lowest_dimensions(dim_scores: dict, potentials: dict) -> list[dict]:
    30→    """Build summary entries for the lowest strict-scoring dimensions."""
    31→    sorted_dims = sorted(
    32→        (
    33→            (name, ds)
    34→            for name, ds in dim_scores.items()
    35→            if ds.get("strict", ds["score"]) < 100
    36→        ),
    37→        key=lambda item: item[1].get("strict", item[1]["score"]),
    38→    )
    39→
    40→    lowest = []
    41→    for name, ds in sorted_dims[:3]:
    42→        strict = ds.get("strict", ds["score"])
    43→        issues = ds.get("failing", 0)
    44→        impact = _dominant_detector_impact(
    45→            dim_scores=dim_scores,
    46→            detectors=ds.get("detectors", {}),
    47→            potentials=potentials,
    48→        )
    49→        is_subjective = "subjective_assessment" in ds.get("detectors", {})
    50→        entry = {
    51→            "name": name,
    52→            "strict": round(strict, 1),
    53→            "failing": issues,
    54→            "impact": round(impact, 1),
    55→        }
    56→        if is_subjective:
    57→            entry["subjective"] = True
    58→            entry["impact_description"] = "re-review to improve"
    59→        lowest.append(entry)
    60→    return lowest

    63→def _biggest_gap_dimensions(dim_scores: dict, state: StateModel) -> list[dict]:
    64→    """Build summary entries for dimensions with the biggest strict gap."""
    65→    biggest_gap = []
    66→    scoped = path_scoped_issues(
    67→        state.get("issues", {}), state.get("scan_path")
    68→    )
    69→    for name, ds in dim_scores.items():
    70→        lenient = ds["score"]
    71→        strict = ds.get("strict", lenient)
    72→        gap = lenient - strict
    73→        if gap > 1.0:
    74→            wontfix_count = sum(
    75→                1
    76→                for f in scoped.values()
    77→                if f["status"] == "wontfix"

    79→            )
    80→            biggest_gap.append(
    81→                {
    82→                    "name": name,
    83→                    "lenient": round(lenient, 1),
    84→                    "strict": round(strict, 1),
    85→                    "gap": round(gap, 1),
    86→                    "wontfix_count": wontfix_count,
    87→                }
    88→            )
    89→    biggest_gap.sort(key=lambda x: -x["gap"])
    90→    return biggest_gap

    93→def _stagnant_dimensions(dim_scores: dict, history: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:

   103→        stagnant.append(

   113→def _recent_dimension_strict_scores(name: str, history: list[dict]) -> list[float]:
   114→    """Collect recent strict score samples for one dimension."""
   115→    scores: list[float] = []
   116→    for history_entry in history[-5:]:
   117→        dim_entry = (history_entry.get("dimension_scores") or {}).get(name)
   118→        if not dim_entry:

   120→        strict_value = dim_entry.get("strict", dim_entry.get("score"))
   121→        if strict_value is not None:

   194→    if status != "fixed" or plan is None:

   196→
   197→    try:

   201→
   202→        git = detect_git_context()
   203→        if not git.available:

   205→
   206→        uncommitted = get_uncommitted_issues(plan)

   209→
   210→        pr_number = config.get("commit_pr", 0)
   211→
   212→        print(colorize("\n  ── Commit Tracking ──────────────────────────", "dim"))
   213→        print(f"  Branch: {git.branch or '?'}    HEAD: {git.head_sha or '?'}")
   214→        if pr_number:
   215→            print(f"  PR: #{pr_number}")
   216→
   217→        _render_uncommitted_block(uncommitted, just_resolved)
   218→        _render_committed_block(plan.get("commit_log", []))
   219→
   220→        template = config.get(
   221→            "commit_message_template",
   222→            "desloppify: {status} {count} issue(s) — {summary}",
   223→        )
   224→        msg = suggest_commit_message(plan, template)
   225→        if msg:
   226→            print("\n  Suggested commit message:")
   227→            print(colorize(f'    "{msg}"', "cyan"))
   228→
   229→        print(colorize("\n  After committing → `desloppify plan commit-log record`", "dim"))
   230→        print(colorize("  ─────────────────────────────────────────────", "dim"))
   231→
   232→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:

     6→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.inputs import gather_subjective_items

    12→
    13→
    14→def select_queue_items(
    15→    state: StateModel,
    16→    *,
    17→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
    18→    plan: dict | None,
    19→    scan_path: str | None,
    20→    status: str,
    21→    threshold: float,
    22→    visibility: str,
    23→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
    24→    """Select the raw queue item list before ranking/finalization."""
    25→    if status == "open" and not opts.chronic:
    26→        snapshot = build_queue_snapshot(
    27→            state,
    28→            options=opts,
    29→            plan=plan,
    30→            target_strict=threshold,
    31→        )
    32→        return filter_snapshot_items(
    33→            items_for_visibility(snapshot=snapshot, visibility=visibility),
    34→            opts,
    35→        )
    36→
    37→    items = build_issue_items(
    38→        state,
    39→        scan_path=scan_path,
    40→        status_filter=status,
    41→        scope=opts.scope,
    42→        chronic=opts.chronic,
    43→    )
    44→    if opts.include_subjective and status == "all":
    45→        items += gather_subjective_items(state, opts, threshold)
    46→    return items
    47→
    48→
    49→def items_for_visibility(*, snapshot, visibility: str) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
    50→    """Select the snapshot partition for one queue surface."""
    51→    if visibility == QueueVisibility.BACKLOG:
    52→        return [dict(item) for item in snapshot.backlog_items]
    53→    return [dict(item) for item in snapshot.execution_items]
    54→
    55→
    56→def filter_snapshot_items(
    57→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
    58→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
    59→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
    60→    """Apply view-local filtering after snapshot partition selection."""
    61→    filtered = items
    62→    if not opts.include_subjective:
    63→        filtered = [
    64→            item for item in filtered
    65→            if item.get("kind") != "subjective_dimension"
    66→        ]
    67→    if opts.scope:
    68→        filtered = [
    69→            item for item in filtered
    70→            if item.get("kind") != "subjective_dimension" or scope_matches(item, opts.scope)
    71→        ]
    72→    return filtered
    73→

    26→def _preserve_integrity_target(state: StateModel) -> float | None:
    27→    """Extract the current subjective integrity target so recompute doesn't erase it."""
    28→    integrity = state.get("subjective_integrity")
    29→    if not isinstance(integrity, dict):
    30→        return None
    31→    raw = integrity.get("target_score")
    32→    if raw is None:
    33→        return None
    34→    try:
    35→        return max(0.0, min(100.0, float(raw)))
    36→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    37→        return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def coerce_assessment_score(value: object) -> float | None:
    41→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float.
    42→
    43→    Returns ``None`` when the value cannot be interpreted as a numeric score
    44→    (e.g. bools, non-numeric strings, missing keys).
    45→    """
    46→    if is_numeric(value):
    47→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))), 1)
    48→    if isinstance(value, dict):
    49→        raw = value.get("score")
    50→        if not is_numeric(raw):
    51→            return None
    52→        return round(max(0.0, min(100.0, float(raw))), 1)
    53→    return None
    54→
    55→
    56→def _mark_stale_assessments_on_review_resolve(
    57→    state: StateModel,
    58→    *,
    59→    status: str,
    60→    resolved_issues: list[dict],
    61→    now: str,
    62→) -> None:
    63→    """Mark subjective assessments as stale when review issues are resolved.
    64→
    65→    The assessment score is preserved (not zeroed) — only a fresh review import
    66→    should change dimension scores.  The stale marker tells the UI to prompt
    67→    for a re-review.
    68→    """
    69→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    70→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    71→        return
    72→
    73→    touched_dimensions: set[str] = set()
    74→    for issue in resolved_issues:
    75→        if issue.get("detector") != "review":
    76→            continue
    77→        dimension = str(issue.get("detail", {}).get("dimension", "")).strip()
    78→        if dimension:
    79→            touched_dimensions.add(dimension)
    80→
    81→    for dimension in sorted(touched_dimensions):
    82→        if dimension not in assessments:
    83→            continue
    84→
    85→        payload = assessments.get(dimension)
    86→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
    87→            payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    88→            payload["refresh_reason"] = f"review_issue_{status}"
    89→            payload["stale_since"] = now
    90→        else:
    91→            assessments[dimension] = {
    92→                "score": coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0,
    93→                "needs_review_refresh": True,
    94→                "refresh_reason": f"review_issue_{status}",
    95→                "stale_since": now,
    96→            }
    97→
    98→
    99→def match_issues(
   100→    state: StateModel, pattern: str, status_filter: str = "open"
   101→) -> list[dict]:
   102→    """Return issues matching *pattern* with the given status."""
   103→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   104→    return [
   105→        issue
   106→        for issue_id, issue in state["issues"].items()
   107→        if not issue.get("suppressed")
   108→        if (status_filter == "all" or issue["status"] == status_filter)
   109→        and _matches_pattern(issue_id, issue, pattern)
   110→    ]
   111→
   112→
   113→def resolve_issues(
   114→    state: StateModel,
   115→    pattern: str,
   116→    status: str,
   117→    note: str | None = None,
   118→    attestation: str | None = None,
   119→) -> list[str]:
   120→    """Set issue status for matches and return affected issue IDs."""
   121→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   122→    now = utc_now()
   123→    resolved: list[str] = []
   124→    resolved_issues: list[dict] = []
   125→
   126→    def _refresh_original_wontfix(issue: dict) -> None:
   127→        if status != "fixed" or issue.get("detector") != "stale_wontfix":
   128→            return
   129→        detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   130→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   131→            return
   132→        original_issue_id = detail.get("original_issue_id")
   133→        if not isinstance(original_issue_id, str) or not original_issue_id:
   134→            return
   135→        original = state["issues"].get(original_issue_id)
   136→        if not isinstance(original, dict) or original.get("status") != "wontfix":
   137→            return
   138→        snapshot_scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   139→        original["wontfix_scan_count"] = snapshot_scan_count
   140→        original["wontfix_snapshot"] = {
   141→            "captured_at": now,
   142→            "scan_count": snapshot_scan_count,
   143→            "tier": original.get("tier"),
   144→            "confidence": original.get("confidence"),
   145→            "detail": copy.deepcopy(original.get("detail", {})),
   146→        }
   147→
   148→    status_filter = "all" if status == "open" else "open"
   149→    for issue in match_issues(state, pattern, status_filter=status_filter):
   150→        previous_status = str(issue.get("status", "open")).strip() or "open"
   151→        if status == "open" and previous_status == "open":
   152→            continue
   153→
   154→        extra_updates: dict[str, object] = {}
   155→        if status == "wontfix":
   156→            snapshot_scan_count = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   157→            extra_updates["wontfix_scan_count"] = snapshot_scan_count
   158→            extra_updates["wontfix_snapshot"] = {
   159→                "captured_at": now,
   160→                "scan_count": snapshot_scan_count,
   161→                "tier": issue.get("tier"),
   162→                "confidence": issue.get("confidence"),
   163→                "detail": copy.deepcopy(issue.get("detail", {})),
   164→            }
   165→        if status == "open":
   166→            issue["reopen_count"] = int(issue.get("reopen_count", 0) or 0) + 1
   167→            issue.pop("wontfix_scan_count", None)
   168→            issue.pop("wontfix_snapshot", None)
   169→            previous_note = issue.get("note")
   170→            next_note = note if note is not None else previous_note
   171→            extra_updates["resolved_at"] = None
   172→            extra_updates["note"] = next_note
   173→            reopen_attestation = {
   174→                "kind": "manual_reopen",
   175→                "text": attestation or note,
   176→                "attested_at": now,
   177→                "scan_verified": False,
   178→            }
   179→            reopen_attestation["previous_status"] = previous_status
   180→            extra_updates["resolution_attestation"] = reopen_attestation

1→"""Dismissal helpers for cluster triage plan mutations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from .prompt import TriageResult
     6→
     7→
     8→def _triaged_out_payload(
     9→    *,
    10→    issue_id: str,
    11→    reason: str,
    12→    note: str | None,
    13→    now: str,
    14→    scan_count: int,
    15→) -> dict:
    16→    return {
    17→        "issue_id": issue_id,
    18→        "kind": "triaged_out",
    19→        "reason": reason,
    20→        "note": note,
    21→        "attestation": None,
    22→        "created_at": now,
    23→        "review_after": None,
    24→        "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
    25→    }
    26→
    27→
    28→def dismiss_triage_issues(
    29→    *,
    30→    triage: TriageResult,
    31→    order: list[str],
    32→    skipped: dict,
    33→    now: str,
    34→    version: int,
    35→    scan_count: int,
    36→) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
    37→    """Move triage-dismissed issues out of queue and into skipped metadata."""
    38→    dismissed_ids: list[str] = []
    39→    dismiss_count = 0
    40→    for dismissed in triage.dismissed_issues:
    41→        issue_id = dismissed.issue_id
    42→        dismissed_ids.append(issue_id)
    43→        if issue_id in order:
    44→            order.remove(issue_id)
    45→        skipped[issue_id] = _triaged_out_payload(
    46→            issue_id=issue_id,
    47→            reason=dismissed.reason,
    48→            note=f"Dismissed by epic triage v{version}",
    49→            now=now,
    50→            scan_count=scan_count,
    51→        )
    52→        dismiss_count += 1
    53→
    54→    for epic_data in triage.clusters:
    55→        for issue_id in epic_data.get("dismissed", []):
    56→            if issue_id in dismissed_ids or issue_id not in order:
    57→                continue
    58→            order.remove(issue_id)
    59→            dismissed_ids.append(issue_id)
    60→            skipped[issue_id] = _triaged_out_payload(
    61→                issue_id=issue_id,
    62→                reason=f"Dismissed by epic triage v{version}",
    63→                note=None,
    64→                now=now,
    65→                scan_count=scan_count,
    66→            )
    67→            dismiss_count += 1
    68→
    69→    return dismissed_ids, dismiss_count
    70→
    71→
    72→__all__ = ["dismiss_triage_issues"]
    73→

    50→def _normalized_epic_name(raw_name: str) -> str:
    51→    return raw_name if raw_name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX) else f"{EPIC_PREFIX}{raw_name}"
    52→
    53→
    54→def _update_existing_epic_cluster(
    55→    existing: Cluster,
    56→    epic_data: dict,
    57→    *,
    58→    now: str,
    59→    version: int,
    60→) -> None:
    61→    existing["thesis"] = epic_data["thesis"]

    64→    existing["issue_ids"] = epic_data["issue_ids"]

    69→    existing["updated_at"] = now
    70→    existing["triage_version"] = version
    71→    existing["description"] = epic_data["thesis"]
    72→    # Don't overwrite in_progress status from agent
    73→    if existing.get("status") != "in_progress":
    74→        existing["status"] = epic_data.get("status", "pending")

   100→        "agent_safe": epic_data.get("agent_safe", False),
   101→        "dependency_order": epic_data["dependency_order"],
   102→        "action_steps": epic_data.get("action_steps", []),
   103→        "source_clusters": [],
   104→        "status": epic_data.get("status", "pending"),
   105→        "triage_version": version,
   106→    }
   107→
   108→
   109→def _upsert_triage_clusters(
   110→    *,
   111→    clusters: dict[str, Cluster],
   112→    triage: TriageResult,
   113→    now: str,
   114→    version: int,
   115→) -> tuple[int, int]:
   116→    created = 0
   117→    updated = 0
   118→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   119→        raw_name = epic_data["name"]
   120→        epic_name = _normalized_epic_name(raw_name)
   121→        existing = clusters.get(epic_name)
   122→        if existing and existing.get("thesis"):
   123→            _update_existing_epic_cluster(existing, epic_data, now=now, version=version)
   124→            updated += 1
   125→            continue
   126→        clusters[epic_name] = _create_epic_cluster(
   127→            epic_name=epic_name,
   128→            epic_data=epic_data,
   129→            now=now,
   130→            version=version,
   131→        )
   132→        created += 1
   133→    return created, updated
   134→
   135→
   136→def _reorder_queue_by_dependency(
   137→    *,
   138→    order: list[str],
   139→    triage: TriageResult,
   140→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   141→) -> None:
   142→    epic_issue_ids: set[str] = set()
   143→    epic_ordered_ids: list[str] = []
   144→    dismissed_set = set(dismissed_ids)
   145→    for epic_data in sorted(triage.clusters, key=_epic_sort_key):
   146→        for fid in epic_data["issue_ids"]:
   147→            if fid in epic_issue_ids or fid in dismissed_set:
   148→                continue
   149→            epic_issue_ids.add(fid)
   150→            epic_ordered_ids.append(fid)
   151→
   152→    non_epic_items = [fid for fid in order if fid not in epic_issue_ids]
   153→    order.clear()
   154→    order.extend(epic_ordered_ids)
   155→    order.extend(non_epic_items)
   156→
   157→
   158→def _set_triage_meta(
   159→    *,
   160→    plan: PlanModel,
   161→    state: StateModel,
   162→    triage: TriageResult,
   163→    now: str,
   164→    version: int,
   165→    dismissed_ids: list[str],
   166→    trigger: str,
   167→) -> None:
   168→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   169→    open_review_ids = sorted(
   170→        fid
   171→        for fid, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   172→        if issue.get("status") == "open"
   173→        and issue.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   174→    )
   175→
   176→    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = {
   177→        "triaged_ids": open_review_ids,
   178→        "last_run": now,
   179→        "version": version,
   180→        "dismissed_ids": dismissed_ids,
   181→        "issue_snapshot_hash": current_hash,
   182→        "strategy_summary": triage.strategy_summary,
   183→        "trigger": trigger,
   184→    }
   185→
   186→
   187→def apply_triage_to_plan(
   188→    plan: PlanModel,
   189→    state: StateModel,
   190→    triage: TriageResult,
   191→    *,
   192→    trigger: str = "manual",
   193→) -> TriageMutationResult:
   194→    """Apply parsed triage result to the living plan.

   196→    1. Creates/updates triage clusters in plan["clusters"]
   197→    2. Marks dismissed issues as triaged_out skips
   198→    3. Reorders queue_order to group cluster members by dependency_order
   199→    4. Updates epic_triage_meta with snapshot hash

1→"""Structural-area reporting helpers for status output."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections import defaultdict
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     8→from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_area
     9→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import path_scoped_issues
    10→
    11→
    12→def collect_structural_areas(
    13→    state: dict,
    14→) -> list[tuple[str, list]] | None:
    15→    """Collect T3/T4 structural issues grouped by area."""
    16→    issues = path_scoped_issues(
    17→        state.get("issues", {}), state.get("scan_path")
    18→    )
    19→    structural = [
    20→        issue
    21→        for issue in issues.values()
    22→        if issue["tier"] in (3, 4) and issue["status"] in ("open", "wontfix")
    23→    ]
    24→    if len(structural) < 5:
    25→        return None
    26→
    27→    areas: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
    28→    for issue in structural:
    29→        area = get_area(str(issue.get("file", "")))
    30→        areas[area].append(issue)
    31→    if len(areas) < 2:
    32→        return None
    33→
    34→    return sorted(areas.items(), key=lambda pair: -sum(f["tier"] for f in pair[1]))
    35→
    36→
    37→def build_area_rows(
    38→    sorted_areas: list[tuple[str, list]],
    39→    *,
    40→    max_areas: int = 15,
    41→) -> list[list[str]]:
    42→    """Build table rows from sorted area issues."""
    43→    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    44→    for area, area_issues in sorted_areas[:max_areas]:
    45→        t3 = sum(1 for issue in area_issues if issue["tier"] == 3)
    46→        t4 = sum(1 for issue in area_issues if issue["tier"] == 4)
    47→        open_count = sum(1 for issue in area_issues if issue["status"] == "open")
    48→        debt_count = sum(1 for issue in area_issues if issue["status"] == "wontfix")
    49→        weight = sum(issue["tier"] for issue in area_issues)
    50→        rows.append(
    51→            [
    52→                area,
    53→                str(len(area_issues)),
    54→                f"T3:{t3} T4:{t4}",
    55→                str(open_count),
    56→                str(debt_count),
    57→                str(weight),
    58→            ]
    59→        )
    60→    return rows

    18→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    19→class ReviewHistoryOptions:

    24→
    25→def _normalize_int(raw: object, *, default: int, minimum: int = 1) -> int:
    26→    try:
    27→        value = int(raw)
    28→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    29→        return default
    30→    return value if value >= minimum else default
    31→
    32→
    33→def _trim(text: object, *, limit: int) -> str:
    34→    value = str(text or "").strip()
    35→    if len(value) <= limit:
    36→        return value
    37→    return value[: max(limit - 3, 0)].rstrip() + "..."
    38→
    39→
    40→def _timestamp_sort_key(value: object) -> tuple[int, str]:
    41→    raw = str(value or "").strip()
    42→    if not raw:
    43→        return (0, "")
    44→    try:
    45→        return (1, datetime.fromisoformat(raw.replace("Z", "+00:00")).isoformat())
    46→    except ValueError:
    47→        return (1, raw)
    48→
    49→
    50→def _issue_dimension(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    51→    detail = issue.get("detail")
    52→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
    53→        return "unknown"
    54→    dimension = str(detail.get("dimension", "")).strip()
    55→    return dimension or "unknown"
    56→
    57→
    58→def _related_files(issue: dict[str, Any], *, limit: int = 6) -> list[str]:
    59→    detail = issue.get("detail")
    60→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
    61→        return []
    62→    raw = detail.get("related_files")
    63→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
    64→        return []
    65→    out: list[str] = []
    66→    seen: set[str] = set()
    67→    for value in raw:
    68→        file_path = str(value or "").strip()
    69→        if not file_path or file_path in seen:
    70→            continue
    71→        seen.add(file_path)
    72→        out.append(file_path)
    73→        if len(out) >= limit:
    74→            break
    75→    return out
    76→
    77→
    78→def _iter_review_issues(state: StateModel) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    79→    issues = state.get("issues")
    80→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    81→        return []
    82→    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    83→    for raw in issues.values():
    84→        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
    85→            continue
    86→        if str(raw.get("detector", "")).strip() != "review":
    87→            continue
    88→        out.append(raw)
    89→    return out
    90→
    91→
    92→def _meaningful_note(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    93→    """Return the note if it's a real human-written note, not an auto-resolve boilerplate."""
    94→    raw = str(issue.get("note", "") or "").strip()
    95→    if not raw or raw == _AUTO_RESOLVE_NOTE:
    96→        return ""
    97→    return raw

   100→def _shape_issue(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   101→    """Shape a single issue into the payload format for the reviewer."""
   102→    detail = issue.get("detail") or {}
   103→    return {
   104→        "dimension": _issue_dimension(issue),
   105→        "status": str(issue.get("status", "open")).strip() or "open",
   106→        "summary": _trim(issue.get("summary", ""), limit=200),
   107→        "suggestion": _trim(detail.get("suggestion", ""), limit=200),
   108→        "related_files": _related_files(issue),
   109→        "note": _meaningful_note(issue),
   110→        "confidence": str(issue.get("confidence", "")).strip(),
   111→        "first_seen": str(issue.get("first_seen", "")).strip(),
   112→        "last_seen": str(issue.get("last_seen", "")).strip(),
   113→    }
   114→
   115→
   116→def build_issue_history_context(
   117→    state: StateModel,
   118→    *,
   119→    options: ReviewHistoryOptions | None = None,
   120→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   121→    """Build flat issue-history context for retrospective subjective review.
   122→
   123→    Returns the most recent review issues as a flat list, each with its
   124→    status, summary, suggestion, related files, and any human-written note.
   125→    """
   126→    resolved_options = options or ReviewHistoryOptions()
   127→    max_issues = _normalize_int(resolved_options.max_issues, default=30)
   128→
   129→    review_issues = _iter_review_issues(state)
   130→    if not review_issues:
   131→        return {
   132→            "summary": {
   133→                "total_review_issues": 0,
   134→                "open_review_issues": 0,
   135→                "status_counts": {status: 0 for status in _KNOWN_STATUSES},
   136→                "dimension_open_counts": {},
   137→            },
   138→            "recent_issues": [],
   139→        }
   140→
   141→    status_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
   142→    dimension_open_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
   143→
   144→    for issue in review_issues:
   145→        status = str(issue.get("status", "open")).strip() or "open"
   146→        status_counts[status] += 1
   147→        if status == "open":
   148→            dimension_open_counts[_issue_dimension(issue)] += 1
   149→
   150→    # Sort by last_seen descending, take the most recent N.
   151→    sorted_issues = sorted(
   152→        review_issues,
   153→        key=lambda f: _timestamp_sort_key(f.get("last_seen")),
   154→        reverse=True,
   155→    )
   156→
   157→    recent_issues = [_shape_issue(f) for f in sorted_issues[:max_issues]]
   158→
   159→    return {
   160→        "summary": {
   161→            "total_review_issues": len(review_issues),
   162→            "open_review_issues": int(status_counts.get("open", 0)),
   163→            "status_counts": {
   164→                status: int(status_counts.get(status, 0)) for status in _KNOWN_STATUSES
   165→            },
   166→            "dimension_open_counts": {
   167→                dim: count
   168→                for dim, count in sorted(
   169→                    dimension_open_counts.items(),
   170→                    key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]),
   171→                )
   172→            },
   173→        },
   174→        "recent_issues": recent_issues,
   175→    }
   176→
   177→
   178→def _normalize_dimensions(dimensions: object) -> list[str]:
   179→    if not isinstance(dimensions, list | tuple | set):
   180→        return []

1→"""Scan-scope helpers shared by state filtering and scoring integration."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import Issue
     6→
     7→
     8→def path_scoped_issues(
     9→    issues: dict[str, Issue],
    10→    scan_path: str | None,
    11→) -> dict[str, Issue]:
    12→    """Filter issues to those within the given scan path."""
    13→    return {
    14→        issue_id: issue
    15→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
    16→        if issue_in_scan_scope(str(issue.get("file", "")), scan_path)
    17→    }
    18→
    19→
    20→def issue_in_scan_scope(file_path: str, scan_path: str | None) -> bool:
    21→    """Return True when a file path belongs to the active scan scope."""
    22→    if not scan_path or scan_path == ".":
    23→        return True
    24→    prefix = scan_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
    25→    return (
    26→        file_path.startswith(prefix)
    27→        or file_path == scan_path
    28→        or file_path == "."
    29→    )
    30→
    31→
    32→def open_scope_breakdown(
    33→    issues: dict[str, Issue],
    34→    scan_path: str | None,
    35→    *,
    36→    detector: str | None = None,
    37→) -> dict[str, int]:
    38→    """Return open-issue counts split by in-scope vs out-of-scope carryover."""
    39→    in_scope = 0
    40→    out_of_scope = 0
    41→
    42→    for issue in issues.values():
    43→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
    44→            continue
    45→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    46→            continue
    47→        if detector is not None and issue.get("detector") != detector:
    48→            continue
    49→        file_path = str(issue.get("file", ""))
    50→        if issue_in_scan_scope(file_path, scan_path):
    51→            in_scope += 1
    52→        else:
    53→            out_of_scope += 1
    54→
    55→    return {
    56→        "in_scope": in_scope,
    57→        "out_of_scope": out_of_scope,
    58→        "global": in_scope + out_of_scope,
    59→    }
    60→
    61→
    62→__all__ = [
    63→    "issue_in_scan_scope",
    64→    "open_scope_breakdown",
    65→    "path_scoped_issues",
    66→]

   236→def ensure_plan_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   237→    """Normalize a loaded plan to ensure all keys exist.
   238→
   239→    Runtime contract is v8-only. Legacy payloads are upgraded in-place once.
   240→    """
   241→    defaults = empty_plan()
   242→    for key, value in defaults.items():
   243→        plan.setdefault(key, value)
   244→    _upgrade_plan_to_v8(plan)
   245→    subjective_defer_meta = plan.get("subjective_defer_meta")
   246→    if isinstance(subjective_defer_meta, dict):
   247→        subjective_defer_meta.pop("force_visible_ids", None)
   248→    epic_triage_meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta")
   249→    if isinstance(epic_triage_meta, dict):
   250→        epic_triage_meta.pop("triage_force_visible", None)

   253→def triage_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   254→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   255→    return {
   256→        name: cluster
   257→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   258→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   259→    }

   261→
   262→def tracked_plan_ids(plan: dict[str, Any] | None) -> set[str]:
   263→    """Collect all issue IDs the plan is actively tracking.
   264→
   265→    Includes queue_order, skipped, overrides, and cluster members/step refs.
   266→    Returns an empty set for None or non-dict plans.
   267→    """
   268→    if not isinstance(plan, dict):
   269→        return set()
   270→    tracked: set[str] = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   271→    tracked.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   272→    tracked.update(plan.get("overrides", {}).keys())
   273→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   274→        tracked.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   275→        for step in cluster.get("action_steps", []):
   276→            if isinstance(step, dict):
   277→                tracked.update(step.get("issue_refs", []))
   278→    return tracked
   279→
   280→
   281→def planned_objective_ids(
   282→    all_objective_ids: set[str],
   283→    plan: dict[str, Any] | None,
   284→) -> set[str]:
   285→    """Return the subset of objective IDs the plan considers active work.
   286→
   287→    Pre-triage (plan tracks nothing): all objective IDs are treated as
   288→    planned work.
   289→
   290→    Once the plan tracks anything, only the intersection with live
   291→    objective IDs counts as planned. This lets stale queue_order entries
   292→    fail closed into postflight/backlog instead of broadening execution
   293→    back out to the entire objective backlog.
   294→    """
   295→    tracked = tracked_plan_ids(plan)
   296→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys()) if isinstance(plan, dict) else set()
   297→    active_tracked = {
   298→        issue_id
   299→        for issue_id in tracked - skipped_ids
   300→        if not any(issue_id.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES)
   301→    }
   302→    if not active_tracked:
   303→        return set(all_objective_ids)
   304→    return all_objective_ids & active_tracked
   305→
   306→
   307→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   308→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   309→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   310→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   311→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   312→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   313→
   314→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   315→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   316→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   317→    if overlap:
   318→        raise ValueError(
   319→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   320→        )
   321→
   322→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   323→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   324→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   325→            raise ValueError(f"plan.skipped[{fid!r}] must be an object")
   326→        if "kind" not in entry:
   327→            raise ValueError(f"plan.skipped[{fid!r}] missing required key 'kind'")
   328→        kind = entry["kind"]
   329→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   330→            raise ValueError(
   331→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   332→            )
   333→
